about.title: Fort Bragg Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Fort Bragg is a town of about 7,289 people on the Mendocino coast, and a single death here is felt on Main Street and in every conversation for weeks. In 2025, public records list 5 injury collisions and 9 people hurt on Fort Bragg roads, with no traffic deaths recorded that year. That number is a relief, but families still lose loved ones to preventable causes: a crash on Route 1 or Franklin Street, a fall on poorly kept property, a medical error, an incident at work. When negligence ends a life, California gives the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain dependents and heirs able to follow. The claim is civil and moves separately from any criminal charge. Recoverable losses cover funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the harder-to-measure loss of love, companionship and guidance. LawProactive connects Fort Bragg families with an independent attorney at no cost, so you can ask questions before deciding anything.

whyChoose.title: Why Fort Bragg Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing, starting with the spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney in our network can explain where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: The two-year clock is real
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Connecting early keeps those deadlines from becoming a second loss.

items.title: Losses measured honestly
items.desc: Recoverable damages include funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. Your attorney works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Fort Bragg recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Does wrongful death still apply here?
items.answer: Yes. Public records show 5 injury collisions and 9 people hurt in Fort Bragg in 2025, with no traffic fatalities, but wrongful death claims are not limited to the roads. They can arise from medical negligence, unsafe property, workplace incidents, or care facility neglect anywhere in Mendocino County. If someone's carelessness contributed to a death, it is worth a conversation.

items.question: What if a city or state agency may share responsibility, such as on Route 1?
items.answer: Claims against a government entity in California follow a much shorter deadline than the standard two years from the date of death. Missing that earlier window can close the door on part of a claim entirely. An attorney can sort out quickly whether a public agency is involved and what timeline applies.

items.question: There is a criminal case pending. Do we have to wait for it to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and proceeds separately from any criminal prosecution. The criminal case is about punishment; the civil claim is about your family's losses, including funeral costs, lost support, and lost companionship. The two can move at the same time, and the outcome of one does not decide the other.
